name: waku
description: Waku Memory: memory that follows you across ChatGPT, Codex, Claude Code and other agents. memory.search finds what you said before; memory.remember keeps what matters. What the agent passes to a tool is sent to Waku's servers and on to the AI providers that make it searchable, named at www.waku.one/privacy. This is an alpha and its data can be lost.

interface.longDescription:
Waku Memory keeps what you tell your AI agents and what they learn, and brings it back in later conversations. One memory store serves ChatGPT, Codex, Claude Code and any other agent that speaks MCP. A preference you state in one of them reaches the others.

Ask "Which package manager should I use?" and ChatGPT searches your memories and answers from them. Say "Remember that I write commit messages in the imperative mood" and ChatGPT saves it. Ask where a memory came from, and ChatGPT shows its origin and every revision. Ask ChatGPT to forget a memory, and it stops coming back.

You sign in with your Waku account. Waku receives only what ChatGPT passes to its tools: your search queries and the memories it saves. Waku sends them on to the AI providers that make memories searchable, named at https://www.waku.one/privacy. This is an alpha, and its data can be lost.

positive.description: Save a new preference the user states.
positive.prompt: Remember that I write commit messages in the imperative mood, like 'Add login page'.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT calls memory.remember with the preference in the user's words and kind preference, then confirms it was saved. Asking a second time returns the existing memory with deduped set to true, so no duplicate is stored.

positive.description: Answer from a preference saved earlier.
positive.prompt: Which package manager should I use for my new JavaScript project?
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT calls memory.search and finds the memory 'Prefers pnpm over npm for JavaScript projects.' It recommends pnpm and says the recommendation comes from that memory.

positive.description: Recall a project decision and its reason.
positive.prompt: What did we decide about the database for Orbit, and why?
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT calls memory.search and finds the Orbit decision. It answers that Orbit uses Postgres, and that MongoDB was rejected in March 2026 because the team needed joins.

positive.description: Explain where a memory came from.
positive.prompt: Where did the rule about releasing Orbit on Tuesdays come from? Has it changed?
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT calls memory.search to find the release rule, then memory.explain with its id. It reports where the memory came from, each revision in order and how often it has been retrieved.

positive.description: Forget a memory after the user confirms.
positive.prompt: Forget the memory that says I use tabs for indentation.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT calls memory.search to find the memory, then asks the user to confirm, because memory.forget is marked destructive. After the user confirms, memory.forget succeeds, and a new search no longer returns the memory.

negative.description: General knowledge does not depend on the user's memories. ChatGPT answers directly and calls no Waku tool.
negative.prompt: What is the capital of Australia?

negative.description: A secret must not be stored. ChatGPT declines to save it, calls no Waku tool, and can suggest a password manager instead.
negative.prompt: Remember my bank card PIN, 4821, so you can remind me later.

negative.description: Live information is outside what Waku holds. ChatGPT calls no Waku tool and answers from a live source or says it has none.
negative.prompt: What's the weather in Tokyo right now?

publication.release_notes: First release in the directory. ChatGPT and Codex can search, save, explain and forget Waku memories, the same memories Claude Code and other agents use. This version runs no hooks, so a memory reaches a conversation only when the model calls a tool.
